angle: The Flatiron Building’s footprint is a scalene right triangle, not the isosceles‑shaped “flat‑iron” most people picture
angle_support: "The Flatiron Building occupies a triangular city block… Despite the building's name, the site is shaped like a scalene right triangle; a genuine flatiron is shaped like an isosceles triangle."
"The Flatiron Building (originally the Fuller Building) is a 22‑story… triangular building… The shape of the site arises from Broadway's diagonal alignment relative to the Manhattan street grid."
title: The Flatiron Building's Secret Geometry
description: We reveal the surprising truth about the Flatiron Building's unique footprint. It turns out the iconic structure isn't the shape you assume it is.
narration: FLATIRON BUILDING IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a classic, symmetric flat-iron. It was closer to a scalene right triangle. The building's footprint defies the simple shape that gave it a famous name. Its sides measure exactly 197.5 feet, 214.5 feet, and 86 feet. Because these edges are unequal, it creates an irregular, slanted profile. A true clothes iron is isosceles, but this skyscraper is mathematically distinct and lopsided. The city grid forced a geometry that never matched its nickname.
